subject: Finova: Decision criteria clarification (latency, deployment, SLA) — Post-call follow-up

Subject: Finova: Decision criteria clarification (latency, deployment, SLA) — Post-call follow-up

Hi Alice / Mark —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the productive call. Quick recap and a few clarification questions so we can pull together the right proposal and next steps:

1) Decision criteria (what Finova told us):
   - Latency target: low p95 for inference (you mentioned "fast enough for interactive UI" — we captured this as ~200–250ms p95)
   - Unit cost expectations: economics for 1M tokens/month workload (you mentioned wanting to keep unit costs competitive)
   - Deployment preference: you said private/VPC is preferred but open to dedicated reserved capacity for early rollout
   - SLA: you flagged availability + incident response time as must-haves (we heard 99.9% or better)

2) Clarifying questions we promised to confirm:
   - Can you confirm the hard latency p95 target we should design to (200ms / 250ms / other)?
   - Is the preferred deployment "Private (customer VPC)" or "Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool)" for the first phase?
   - Who is the economic buyer and who owns procurement/legal/security conversations we should loop in?

3) Next steps we propose:
   - Send our SLA draft + SOC2 / security artifacts and a short performance profile for the recommended config (attached)
   - Schedule a 30-min follow-up with procurement and security to walk the questionnaire and timeline

Attachments: redwood-performance-profile.pdf (performance expectations), SOX_questionnaire.pdf (vendor questionnaire template)

If you can confirm the three items above and share the right procurement/security contact, we'll convert this into a scoped proposal with rough pricing and an implementation plan.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Finova: Decision criteria clarification (latency, deployment, SLA) — Post-call follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the summary and for the docs. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: Our product team needs p95 inference latency under 250ms for the primary UI (average prompt length ~200 tokens). If you can hit ~200ms p95 that's a nice-to-have but 250ms is the hard cutoff.
- Cost: We're targeting an operational cost that keeps model inference below ~$1500 per 1M tokens consumed (ballpark for vendor comparison).
- Deployment: For security reasons we prefer Private (customer VPC) long-term. For the pilot we are open to Dedicated reserved capacity managed by you if that reduces time-to-value, but the plan should include an eventual VPC/private deployment path.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime is the baseline we need; we also care about RTO for incident response (2 hours initial response desirable). Can you indicate whether Redwood offers 99.9% as standard for Dedicated and what higher tiers look like?

Please loop in our security lead Priya Singh (priya.singh@finova.com) for the questionnaire and procurement timelines — Priya will be the point for security evidence and legal. Procurement timeline: we expect vendor selection + contract within ~6–8 weeks after the pilot if things look good.

I've attached our current security requirements spreadsheet and the questionnaire we typically use (Finova_security_requirements.xlsx).

Thanks,
Mark Roberts
VP Product — Finova
mark.roberts@finova.com

Attachment: Finova_security_requirements.xlsx

Subject: Re: Finova: Decision criteria clarification (latency, deployment, SLA) — Technical follow-up

Thanks Mark — quick technical answers to help scope the pilot and the eventual VPC deployment: 

1) Latency by deployment mode (typical for models with ~200-token prompts):
   - Hosted (multi-tenant): p95 ~= 220–300ms depending on model size and burst. Not guaranteed for strict SLOs.
   - Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPUs): p95 ~= 140–220ms tuned (can reliably hit ~180ms p95 with the configs below).
   - Private (customer VPC / on-prem): performance depends on customer infra; we recommend equivalent GPU class and network setup to Dedicated for parity.

2) Recommended pilot config to meet 250ms p95 target and show headroom:
   - Model variant: (redwood-curated) gpt-large-1 or equivalent open model; sequence length cap 512 tokens
   - Dedicated pool: 4x A100 (or 2x A100 with aggressive batching) with continuous batching disabled for interactive latency
   - KV cache + prefix caching enabled for conversational flows

Estimated sample performance (approx):
   - Dedicated (4x A100): p50 ~45ms, p95 ~170–190ms
   - Cost estimate: ~ $1,100–$1,600 per 1M tokens depending on batching and utilization (pilot assumes low utilization -> higher per-token cost). We'll provide a more detailed run-rate once we have exact token profile.

3) SLA / incident response:
   - Redwood Dedicated: standard SLA 99.9% uptime. Premium SLA 99.95% available with higher committed capacity and dedicated on-call routing (adds ~10–15% to committed price). Initial response SLOs can be contractually defined (we can meet 2-hour initial response as an addendum).

4) Security artifacts we can share immediately: SOC 2 Type II report excerpt, pen-test summary, encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, and an audit log sample. We'll drop the artifacts into the shared link once you confirm access.

I'll build a short proposal PDF showing the recommended Dedicated pilot config + rough pricing bands and two migration paths (1) start Dedicated -> migrate to Private VPC; (2) start Private pilot (longer lead time).

Let me know if you want us to include an A/B of model sizes (throughput-aware vs latency-focused) in the proposal.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Deployment: Pilot recommended on Dedicated (shorter lead time). Plan includes migration path to Private/VPC for production.
- SLA: Standard Dedicated SLA = 99.9%; we can offer 99.95% as premium. We can include a 2-hour initial response commitment in the contract.
